### Loading a track {modern}

There are three ways to load the highlighted track:

```nav browse-load Loading a track {modern}
```

- Tap the row, then tap **1** or **2** on its LOAD chip.
- Push the encoder twice to load on the active deck, or push, turn to another deck and push.
- Press the [[LOAD]] button of the deck you want.

If no track is highlighted, [[LOAD]] says **SELECT A TRACK, THEN PRESS LOAD**. On a screen that is not a track list it says **OPEN A TRACK LIST TO LOAD**. To load onto decks 3 and 4, see [Four decks](four-decks).

### Playlists {modern}

Tap **PLAYLIST** in the BROWSE category rail, or on the SHORTCUT screen, to open the USB's playlists. You can also make your own and change them on the player. Press [[MENU]] in the playlist list or inside a playlist.

```nav playlists Playlists {modern}
```

| In the MENU panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| NEW PLAYLIST | Makes a playlist in the folder that is open. Type its name on the keyboard |
| RENAME | Renames the highlighted playlist |
| DELETE | Deletes the highlighted playlist. Push again to confirm |
| ADD TO PLAYLIST | Adds the highlighted track to a playlist you pick |
| REMOVE FROM PLAYLIST | Takes the highlighted track out of the playlist |
| MOVE TRACK | Picks up a track. Turn the encoder to move it, push to drop it |

Playlists, the tag list, played marks and histories can change only on a USB that is not read-only. Changes made on the player are saved on the same USB in `XZMODS/playlists.txt`. They never change the library your DJ software exported, so your DJ software and the CLASSIC browse screens do not show them. A playlist you changed on the player is marked in the list. In HISTORY the [[MENU]] panel offers DELETE HISTORY and DELETE ALL HISTORIES, each after a second push. If the USB is read-only you see **THIS STICK IS READ-ONLY: PLAYLISTS CANNOT CHANGE**. If it is full you see **THE STICK IS FULL: PLAYLIST NOT SAVED**.

## Browsing in CLASSIC {classic}

CLASSIC keeps the player's own browse screens: the same lists, keys and menus the XDJ-XZ operating instructions describe. XZ Mods adds three things to them.

- **The key in every row.** Each track row shows up to three fields from the library exported to your USB inside the title cell. The default is the title, then the key, then the BPM.
- **Key before title.** With **KEY BEFORE TITLE** on, the key leads the row, so you can read keys down the list.
- **Key match colours.** With **KEY MATCH COLOURS** on, a leading key is green when it mixes with the master deck's key, amber when it is detuned against it, and grey otherwise.

The table header names what the player's own [[MENU]] click changes: **SORT** over the title column and **COLUMN** over the right-hand column. The STEMS and MODS buttons stay at the top right.

These additions only use tracks on a USB with an exported library. A track XZ Mods cannot match in the export keeps the player's own row, and a field the export does not have is left out.

## Browse settings

```nav nav-a-browse-settings Browse settings
```

| Setting | MODS | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `browse_preview` | PREVIEW tile in MODERN browse | Shows the preview waveform column in MODERN browse | Hidden |
| `browse_traffic` | **SCREEN**, KEY MATCH COLOURS | Colours keys that mix with the master deck's key, in both interfaces | On |
| `browse_key_prefix` | **SCREEN**, KEY BEFORE TITLE | Puts the key first in each CLASSIC browse row | On |
| `browse_1`, `browse_2`, `browse_3` | none | The three fields in each CLASSIC browse row, in order. Each is TITLE, ARTIST, KEY or BPM | TITLE, KEY, BPM |
| `modern_browse_columns` | COLUMNS in the MODERN [[MENU]] panel | The columns of the MODERN track list. TITLE always shows | Automatic |

MODS has no control for the three CLASSIC row fields in this version. They keep the values stored on the USB. In MODERN, choose columns from the [[MENU]] panel instead.

## DJ profile

A DJ profile is your DJ name and logo, with an optional tagline. It lives on your USB, next to your music. VJ software such as VJ.Tools shows the profile of the USB that is playing on the master deck, so the screens behind you show who is playing. Nothing is stored on the XZ and nothing is uploaded.

```nav dj-profile DJ profile
```

DJ Profile is an open standard. Any player, mixer or VJ program can read the same folder.

### Make a profile on a computer

```nav b-profile-rescan Make a profile on a computer
```

1. On the USB, make a folder named `DJPROFILE` at the top level.
2. Inside it, make a folder with your DJ name, for example `DJPROFILE/DJ Kai`.
3. Put your logo in that folder as `logo.png` or `logo.jpg`.
4. Put the USB in the XZ, open **CONNECT** › **DJ PROFILE** and push **CHECK USB FOR PROFILES**.

A folder with a usable logo is a profile. A folder without one is skipped. A USB shows at most 16 profiles. The XZ Mods app can also make and edit profiles. See [The XZ Mods app](desktop-app).

### Make a profile on the XZ

You can type a profile on the player with the encoder or by touch.

```nav dj-profile-create-switch Make a profile on the XZ
```

1. Open **CONNECT** › **DJ PROFILE**.
2. Push **CREATE ON THIS XZ**, or **NEW PROFILE** if the USB already has one.
3. Type your DJ name on the on-screen keyboard, then push **NEXT: LOGO**.
4. Pick a PNG or JPEG image from the USB, or **NO LOGO**. Images in your own `DJPROFILE` folder are listed first. Then push **NEXT: TAGLINE**.
5. Type a few words, such as your genre, city or crew, and push **NEXT: REVIEW**. To leave the tagline out, push **SKIP TAGLINE**.
6. Check the review, then push **SAVE TO USB 1** or **SAVE TO USB 2**.

A new profile becomes the active profile on the USB you save it to. Only the `DJPROFILE` folder on that USB is written. Your music, playlists and stems are not touched.

| Step | Controls |
|---|---|
| Name and tagline | The keyboard, **SHIFT** for capitals, **#+=** for symbols (**ABC** goes back), **SPACE**, **DELETE**, **BACK** to the step before |
| Logo | One row per image on the USB, **PREV** and **NEXT** for more, **RESCAN** (or **CHECK USB AGAIN**), **NO LOGO**, **KEEP CURRENT** when you edit |
| Review | **CHANGE NAME**, **CHANGE LOGO**, **CHANGE TAGLINE**, then **SAVE TO USB 1** or **SAVE TO USB 2** |

- A name holds up to 64 characters and a tagline up to 80.
- With **NO LOGO**, your initial is shown on the accent colour.
- Logos are shown square over black.
- Nothing is saved until you push SAVE. The bottom line says **NOTHING IS SAVED UNTIL YOU PRESS SAVE** on the review step.

### Choose and switch profiles

With profiles on the USB, the DJ PROFILE page shows one profile at a time: its logo, name and tagline, which USB it is on, and whether it is active there.

| Control or line | What it means |
|---|---|
| **< PREV**, **NEXT >** | Step through the profiles on both USBs. **2 OF 3** shows where you are |
| **EDIT** | Change this profile's name, logo or tagline |
| **MAKE ACTIVE** | Makes this the active profile on its USB. Only the USB is written |
| **NEW PROFILE** | Makes another profile on the USB, for an alias or a back to back set |
| **CHECK USB** | Reads both USB ports again |
| ACTIVE ON THIS USB | This profile is the one its USB says is playing |
| SHOWN TO THE VJ NOW | This is the profile VJ software sees right now |
| FROM ITS FOLDER IN DJPROFILE | A profile made from a folder and a logo |
| OLDER CARD: EDIT IT IN VJ.TOOLS | An older profile card. Edit it in VJ.Tools, or make a new profile |

Your active profile also sits in the MODS header, with its logo and name. Tap it, or highlight it and push, to switch between the profiles on both USBs.

> **Note.** The player's own saved settings are MY SETTINGS in UTILITY. They are separate from your DJ profile.

The XZ Mods app runs on your computer. It puts XZ Mods on a USB, makes stems for your tracks, makes your DJ profile, keeps the app and your USB up to date, holds tools for your library, games and the XZ screen, and sends your reports and ideas to the maintainer. It never formats a drive and never changes your music or the library your DJ software exported.

You need 64-bit Windows with WebView2, or a Mac with macOS 14 or later. Making stems needs a Windows computer or an Apple silicon Mac. On an Intel Mac you can still import stems you made elsewhere.

## Around the app

The bar along the top has five sections for your work, then the Manual and About and, on the right, Feedback. The section you are in is filled yellow. The page sits on the raised panel below it.

## Desktop language

Choose **Language / Idioma** below the navigation to open XZ language setup. It detects the bundled offline catalogs, lets you choose a language, imports an optional JSON catalog, then applies the text so you can verify it on screen. No account or translation service is required. This setting belongs to XZ Mods only.

Coverage counts describe extracted desktop and manual text. Machine translations require language review. Export a catalog to review text offline; import rejects changed sources, missing placeholders and altered printed control names. After a source change, regenerate all languages against a fresh source snapshot.

For local generation, open the independent provider section. Detect saved resources, enter the Python executable and Small100 model folder, then choose **Connect and live verify**. The test translates a sentence into all 14 languages. **Install pinned dependencies** creates an XZ-only Python environment using the selected Python and installs the pinned provider packages. It needs network access for those packages, but translation runs locally without credentials or paid services. The Small100 folder must already contain model.bin, shared_vocabulary.json and sentencepiece.bpe.model.

Choose **Generate all languages** to resume the full corpus. Progress and logs remain in the XZ application data directory. **Cancel translation** stops this job and retains checkpoints. Publication replaces the complete language set only after every locale passes structural validation. This does not establish native-speaker approval. The packaged source snapshot belongs to this XZ release; updating the app supplies a new snapshot.

Printed hardware names such as [[CUE]], [[SHIFT]], [[SYNC]], [[MENU]] and [[BACK]] stay as printed. Track names and stock alerts are not translated. Arabic uses browser right-to-left text layout; fonts come from the operating system. Controller screenshots keep their original labels. Controller mod text still needs Unicode font and layout integration; choosing a desktop language does not change it.

Four decks adds two software players, DECK 3 and DECK 4, to the XDJ-XZ's own DECK 1 and DECK 2. You hear them on mixer channels CH3 and CH4. A short USB cable from the back of the player to a top USB port carries their sound into the mixer: it leaves through a top USB port and comes back in at the rear USB socket, where a computer with DJ software would connect. The physical controls switch between decks with the same presses DJ software uses on the XDJ-XZ.

```explainer loopback-signal How the sound of decks 3 and 4 reaches the mixer
Decks 3 and 4 | Decks 3 and 4 are software players. They run inside the player, beside decks 1 and 2.
Top USB | Their sound leaves the player through the top USB port the cable is in, USB 1 or USB 2.
Loopback cable | The loopback cable carries it over the back edge of the player.
Rear USB | It comes back in at the rear USB socket, where a computer with DJ software would connect.
CH3 and CH4 | With their input switches on USB, mixer channels CH3 and CH4 play decks 3 and 4.
```

## What you need {experimental}

- The **loopback cable**: a USB cable with a USB-B plug on one end and a USB-A plug on the other, the kind a printer uses.
- For tracks, a **music stick** in the other top USB port, or music sticks on one **USB 2.0 hub** in that port. Decks 3 and 4 can start before you insert any music.
- Decks 1 and 2 **stopped or paused** while decks 3 and 4 start. Once they run, you can play all four decks.
- **CH3** and **CH4** on the mixer set to **USB** so you hear decks 3 and 4.

The cable goes directly from the rear USB socket to either **USB 1** or **USB 2** on top. Put music in the other top port. The picture uses USB 1 as an example; both arrangements work.

## Set up four decks {experimental}

```nav nav-a-route-rescan Set up four decks
```

```explainer four-deck-setup Set up four decks, step by step
```

1. Stop or pause decks 1 and 2.
2. Choose either top USB port for the loopback cable. Leave the other port for music.
3. Plug the USB-B end of the loopback cable into the **rear USB socket**.
4. Plug the USB-A end directly into your chosen top port, **USB 1** or **USB 2**.
5. Set the **CH3** and **CH4** input switches to **USB**.
6. Tap **DECKS** at the top of the play screen and choose one of the **4 DECKS** pictures, or open MODS and choose [4 DECKS](mods-menu#4-decks).
7. Wait for **DECKS 3 AND 4 ARE READY**. The card in the lanes of decks 3 and 4 tells you each step it is waiting for.
8. Press [[SHIFT]] twice on the left side to play deck 3, or on the right side to play deck 4.

Decks 3 and 4 start as soon as the cable is in, even when decks 1 and 2 have no tracks loaded. You can leave the cable connected before starting the USB loader. No **RESCAN** is needed. Decks 1 and 2 must be stopped or paused while the route starts. **RESCAN** checks at once if you want to check again. After a disconnection, plug the cable back into either top port. Decks 3 and 4 come back once decks 1 and 2 are stopped or paused; the card says when it is waiting for that. No restart of the USB loader is needed, also when you move the cable to the other port.

> **Note.** The [XZ Mods app](desktop-app#four-decks-in-the-app) shows steps 2 to 5 with an animation of the cable while it writes your USB and when it is done. You set four decks up at the player, not in the app.

> **Tip.** You can choose a four-deck view before you plug in the cable. Decks 3 and 4 then show a card with the cable steps and their current state, and decks 1 and 2 keep playing as usual.

## Add music and a USB hub {experimental}

Once the USB loader is running, you can bring up decks 3 and 4 with only the loopback cable connected. Insert music later in the other top port. Starting the audio route does not load a track.

To connect several music sticks, put one high-speed USB 2.0 hub in the top port opposite the loopback cable. Stop or pause decks 1 and 2 while a newly connected hub starts. Connect the sticks to that hub and choose the sources the player makes available. The hub does not add more decks or source buttons.

Connect the loopback cable directly to the player, never through the music hub. Do not connect a second hub behind the first. Check that your hub and drives have enough power; use the hub's own power supply if it has one. Keep any drive that holds a playing track connected.

### The E-8307 hub warning {experimental}

The player sees the loopback cable as a USB hub. When you plug it in, the player raises its own warning **E-8307: HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED** and would keep it up while the cable stays in. ### SYNC on decks 3 and 4 {experimental}

Press [[SYNC]] and the deck takes the master deck's BPM at once. The SYNC button stays lit for as long as SYNC is on. With QUANTIZE on and a beat grid on both tracks, the deck also locks to the master's beat. Press [[SYNC]] again to turn it off.

```explainer sync-master SYNC on deck 3
Master | Deck 1 is the tempo master. Deck 3 plays at its own tempo, with SYNC off.
SYNC | Press [[SYNC]] on deck 3. It takes the master's BPM at once and reads SYNC 1. With QUANTIZE on and a beat grid on both tracks, it also locks to the master's beat.
Tempo only | With QUANTIZE off, only the tempo follows, and deck 3 reads BPM 1.
```

If the beats drift apart, press [[SYNC]] off and on again. With QUANTIZE on, every engage snaps to the nearest position at the selected beat value, even for a small drift. The beat value can be 1, 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 beat. With QUANTIZE off, only the tempo follows.

- The tempo follows even when the master or the synced deck is paused. If the beat position is available, the paused deck aligns once. If it is unavailable, alignment happens as soon as it can be read. Continuous beat lock resumes when both decks play.
- A pause, a jump, a loop or a new master never turns SYNC off. The deck follows again on its own, with no second press.
- Nudge the jog from the side to move the deck a little off the master's beat. SYNC stays on and the tempo stays matched. The deck keeps the new alignment, also when the master's tempo changes, and the [[SYNC]] button flashes.
- Nudge the master's jog from the side to move only the master. It stays master, and the synced decks keep their tempo and the new alignment.
- To line the beats up again, press [[SYNC]] off and on. The deck snaps to the nearest beat and the button lights steadily.
- Scratching on the platter top takes control of the deck. When you let go, QUANTIZE snaps it back to the beat.
- Press [[SYNC]] off and the deck keeps its position and the synced tempo. The tempo fader takes over once you move it to that tempo.
- The tempo fader does not move the deck while SYNC is on.

## Limits

- Decks 1 and 2 must be stopped or paused while decks 3 and 4 start.
- Keep the music stick connected while you play. Decks 3 and 4 read from it all the time.
- Decks 3 and 4 play WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis files. AAC and M4A files do not play on decks 3 and 4.
- A deck 3 or 4 master reads MASTER when decks 1 and 2 can follow it too, and 3/4 MASTER when it drives decks 3 and 4 only.
- Press [[MASTER]] on a playing deck 3 or 4 and it is master at once. The MASTER buttons show the change.
- When you pause the master, MASTER passes at once to the next playing deck. A deck with SYNC on comes first. Otherwise after deck 3 comes deck 4, then decks 1 and 2. After deck 4 come decks 1 and 2, then deck 3. In VINYL mode MASTER passes when you press pause, while the deck slows down.
- When you pause a deck 1 or 2 master, a playing deck 3 or 4 takes MASTER at once. If the other of decks 1 and 2 is playing, MASTER goes to that deck instead, as with two decks.
- In VINYL mode, hold the master's platter top and MASTER passes to the other synced, playing deck after a moment.
- Load a new track on the master and MASTER passes to the other playing deck. The loading deck keeps SYNC on and plays its new track at the tempo the decks shared.
- A handover never changes the tempo.
- A master set by another player over LINK is never taken.
- Some lamps on the player do not yet light as they do for decks 1 and 2. The beat loop and slip loop pad colours are provisional.
- Four decks, the handover of MASTER between native and software decks, and scratching on decks 3 and 4 are experimental in this version.

If something goes wrong, the card or the 4 DECKS page names the state. [Messages and troubleshooting](troubleshooting) lists every notice.

XZ Mods is software for the XDJ-XZ that starts from a USB stick. It adds a MODS menu, stems you can mute live, custom beat jump, four decks over a loopback cable, DJ profiles, themes and games. It can also replace the whole play screen with its own MODERN interface.

## What changes and what stays stock

XZ Mods runs in the player's memory. It never writes to the player's firmware, so the XDJ-XZ itself stays stock.

```nav utility What changes and what stays stock
```

- The player picks up the XZ Mods loader (`autoexec.bin`) from the USB at start and runs XZ Mods from there.
- Your music, the library your DJ software exported and your playlists stay as they are. XZ Mods adds its own folders beside them.
- The player's own settings are still there. Hold [[MENU]] to open UTILITY, exactly as on a stock XDJ-XZ.
- Settings you change in MODS are saved on the USB, so they travel with it to another XZ running XZ Mods.

### Go back to stock

1. Switch the player off.
2. Start it without the XZ Mods USB, or with a USB that has no `autoexec.bin` on it.

The player starts stock. Plug the XZ Mods USB back in and start again to load XZ Mods. If you play from a separate music stick, that stick works on the stock player as before.

## What you need

| Item | What you need |
|---|---|
| Player | XDJ-XZ on firmware 1.26. No other firmware version is supported |
| Computer | 64-bit Windows with WebView2, or a Mac with macOS 14 or later, to prepare the USB |
| Stems | Made on a Windows computer or an Apple silicon Mac. An Intel Mac can import stems made elsewhere |
| USB | A USB stick for the loader. It can be your music USB, or a separate loader stick |
| Four decks | A USB-B to USB-A cable. See [Four decks](four-decks#what-you-need) {experimental} |

The app downloads the official firmware it needs from the manufacturer and checks it. No firmware or boot files come with the XZ Mods download.

> **Caution.** XZ Mods is a preview. Test every new USB at home before you use it in a set.

You prepare the USB in the XZ Mods app on your computer. It does not format the drive or touch your music.

## Saving to the USB

There is no save button in MODS. Every change saves on its own to the settings USB, the stick you browse. The settings live in the VJ.Tools folder on that stick, so they travel with you to another XZ running XZ Mods. When you browse a stick, the player takes that stick's settings. A stick with no settings, or with damaged ones, leaves the current settings as they are.

```nav b-save-recovery Saving to the USB
```

The XZ also remembers the last settings it applied. If you start it with no stick, it uses them.

The save state at the right of the dock says what happened to your last change:

| Save state | What it means |
|---|---|
| SAVING... | The change is being written. |
| SAVED TO USB 1 (or USB 2) | The change is on the stick. |
| SAVED ON THIS XZ / NO USB | No stick is in. The change is kept on this XZ. |
| SAVED ON THIS XZ / USB CHANGED | The settings stick changed. The change is kept on this XZ. |
| SAVED ON THIS XZ / USB PROFILE KEPT | The stick is locked. The change is kept on this XZ and the stick is left as it was. |
| USB REMOVED: SETTINGS KEPT | You pulled the settings stick. Nothing resets. |
| NOT SAVED TO USB 1: CHECK USB | Writing failed. Check that the stick is in and not locked. |
| NOT SAVED: USB PROFILE KEPT | The stick is locked and the XZ could not keep the change either. |
| NO SETTINGS USB: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF. | Nothing can be saved. Your change works until you switch the player off. |
| NOT SAVED: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF. | This build does not save settings. Changes work until you switch the player off. |

Lines that say NOT SAVED or NO SETTINGS USB show in amber. DJ profiles are not settings. They stay on the DJ's stick and never on the XZ. See [Connect and DJ profiles](connect).

## Keys and KEY SYNC

XZ Mods can move the key of any deck a semitone at a time, and match a deck's key to the master deck with KEY SYNC. The master can be any deck, 1 to 4. The key display then shows the key the track plays in now.

```nav keys Keys and KEY SYNC | In MODS
physical-key-sync | KEY SYNC on the deck
```

### From the deck

1. Load tracks with analysed keys, and make the deck you want to match to the tempo master.
2. Hold [[SHIFT]] and press [[SYNC]] on the deck you want to move. On a side that drives deck 3 or 4, this moves that deck.
3. The deck shifts to a key that fits the master deck and MASTER TEMPO turns on. A notice shows the new key and the master deck, with RELATIVE KEY when it matches the relative major or minor.

To end KEY SYNC, press [[SHIFT]] + [[SYNC]] again, or press [[MASTER TEMPO]]. Both return the deck to its own key and put MASTER TEMPO back the way it was. After that, [[MASTER TEMPO]] works as on a stock player.

KEY SYNC changes the key only. The tempo, SYNC and the master deck stay as they were.

All four decks can hold key shifts and KEY SYNC together. Before starting a new shift on deck 3 or 4, the player checks its measured audio workload. If there is too little headroom, it shows **KEY SHIFT REFUSED: AUDIO LOAD TOO HIGH** and leaves the current keys unchanged. Shifts already in use keep running. SYSTEM READOUT shows render times and the number of active key shifters.

If KEY SYNC cannot work, a notice or the deck's key display shows why for a few seconds:

| LOAD AN ANALYZED TRACK / SET UP KEYS | The deck has no track with an analysed key. Load one. |
| LOAD A KEYED TRACK ON DECK 2 (or another deck) | The master deck has no track with an analysed key. |
| THIS DECK IS MASTER, MAKE DECK 2 MASTER FIRST | The deck you pressed is the master, so there is nothing to match. Make another deck the master. On the KEYS page the master deck has no KEY SYNC button and says it is the master. |

### Key and KEY SYNC {modern}

The large key in each deck's column is the key the deck plays right now. Tempo with MASTER TEMPO off, a key shift and KEY SYNC all move it. Its colour compares it with the master deck's key. Green means it mixes with the master's key: the same key, its relative major or minor, or one step away on the key wheel, tuned within 25 cents of the master. Amber means it would mix, but it is detuned by more than 25 cents. White means neither, and the master deck itself is always white. Turn KEY MATCH COLOURS off in **SCREEN** and every key is white. The cents beside it show how far it sits off the semitone, so you can match by ear. Once the playing key leaves the track's analysed key, ORIGINAL shows the analysed key below it.

**SYSTEM READOUT** puts CPU load, memory and temperature beside **STEMS** and **MODS** on the top bar. Open it to see deck 3 and 4 audio render times and active key shifters across all four decks. XZ Mods keeps its settings on your USB, so they travel with you from player to player. This page explains where they are kept and what happens when the USB changes, then lists every setting with its values, its default and the chapter that explains it.

## Where settings are kept

Your settings live in one file on the USB: `VJ.Tools/XZ-Mods.cfg`. You change them in MODS, or on your computer with the [XZ Mods app](desktop-app). There is no save button. Every change saves on its own to the USB you are browsing, and the bottom of the MODS page says what happened for a few seconds.

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| SAVED TO USB 1 (or USB 2) | The change is on that USB. |
| NOT SAVED TO USB 1: CHECK USB | The USB could not be written. Check that it is not full or locked, then change the setting again. |
| SAVED ON THIS XZ / NO USB | No USB is in. The change is kept on this player only. |
| USB REMOVED: SETTINGS KEPT | You pulled the USB. The player keeps your settings for the rest of the set. |
| USB 1 HAS NO SETTINGS: KEPT CURRENT | The USB you browsed has no settings file. The player keeps the settings it has. |
| USB 1 SETTINGS INVALID: KEPT CURRENT | The settings file on that USB could not be read. The player keeps the settings it has. |
| NOT SAVED: CHANGES LAST UNTIL POWER OFF. | This start of XZ Mods cannot save. Your changes work until you switch the player off. |

## When the USB changes

The player follows the same rules as its own MY SETTINGS:

- Browsing a USB in USB 1 or USB 2 loads that USB's settings. Browsing a computer or a LINK source never changes them.
- A USB without settings, or with settings the player cannot read, leaves your current settings as they are. Nothing resets to defaults in the middle of a set.
- The player remembers the last settings it used. Started without a USB, it uses those. A USB with its own settings takes over again once you browse it.

The player's own MY SETTINGS, which your DJ software writes to the USB, are a separate set. XZ Mods settings never change them, and loading MY SETTINGS does not change XZ Mods settings.

MODERN's own display choices are settings too: its waveform colour, waveform position and zoom, how it writes keys, the TRACK COLOURS choice, the LAMPS AND TITLES and BYPASS BUTTON switches, and the columns of its track list. So are the 3-band colours. They are saved to the USB with everything else and come back after the player restarts.

Things you do during a set, such as muting a stem, BYPASS, a key shift, KEY SYNC or a RAM copy, are not settings. They start fresh every time the player starts.

## Going back to the defaults

There is no single button that resets every setting. Set each one back in MODS, using the Default column below. Some pages have their own way back: PAGE 1: STOCK for beat jump page 1, RESET STEM COLORS for the stem colours, and RESET 3-BAND COLOURS for the 3-band colours.

> **Note.** Deleting the settings file from the USB does not reset anything. The player keeps the settings it has, and saves them to the USB again with your next change.

Stems split a track into its parts so you can mute them live. XZ Mods plays three stems per track: **VOCALS**, **HARMONICS** (everything melodic that is not a voice) and **DRUMS**. You mute them from the pads or from buttons on the screen, change their levels by sliding, and switch back to the whole track with **BYPASS**. Stems work on decks 1 and 2. ## Prepare stems

The player cannot split a track itself. You prepare stems on your computer, once per track, and they travel on the USB beside your music.

1. Prepare the stems in the XZ Mods app on your computer, or in OverCue Desktop. See [The XZ Mods app](desktop-app).
2. Keep the stems on the same USB as the music. Your original files and the library your DJ software exported stay unchanged.
3. On the player, load the original track through the normal browser and wait a moment for its stems to load.

A track without prepared stems plays as normal. Its stem buttons say why, and the button at their end tells you what to do (see [Stem readiness](#stem-readiness)).

This chapter lists every message XZ Mods can show you, what it means and the one thing to do about it. Find the words you see on the screen in the tables below. Messages in capitals come from the player. Messages in normal case come from the XZ Mods app on your computer.

## If the player will not start with the USB

XZ Mods never changes the player's firmware, so the player always starts stock without the USB.

```nav updates If the player will not start with the USB
```

1. Switch the player off.
2. Remove the XZ Mods USB and switch the player on. It starts stock. Play from a stick without XZ Mods if you are in a set.
3. On your computer, open the USB in the XZ Mods app. If it says **Update available**, choose **Update USB**. If it says **Up to date**, open **Updates** › **XZ Mods version** › **Restore or update a loader by hand** and update the loader again. The app keeps a backup of the old loader each time.
4. Try the USB again. If it still does not start, [report the problem](#report-a-problem).

Check these first:

| Check | Why |
|---|---|
| The player runs firmware 1.26 | XZ Mods supports no other firmware version |
| `autoexec.bin` is at the top of the USB | A loader prepared into a folder has to be copied to the USB yourself |
| You updated the USB after updating the app | An app update does not change the USB |

If XZ Mods started after a network update and stopped working, open **CONNECT** › **UPDATES** and push **PREVIOUS VERSION**, then switch the player off and on. See [Updates over the network](connect#updates-over-the-network).

If the sound goes wrong while you test, stop playback and switch the player off and on. Load the same track again and check the original mix before you go on.

> **Tip.** MODS is always reachable with the hardware alone. In CLASSIC, the button above [[LINK]] switches to MODERN, where [[MENU]] opens MODS. Turn the encoder to move, push it to choose and press [[BACK]] to go back.

The player sees the loopback cable for four decks as a hub. It raises **E-8307: HUBS ARE NOT SUPPORTED** or **E-8307: UNSUPPORTED DEVICE** and would keep it up while the cable is in. ## The diary on your USB sticks

XZ Mods keeps a short diagnostic diary in `VJ.Tools/XZ-Mods-diary/` on each mounted USB stick, including music sticks. If a problem happens during a set, keep those sticks so you can include their diaries in a later report.

The diary records the XZ Mods version, settings fingerprint, USB slots, interface, deck view, state changes and fixed notice codes. It also records available CPU, memory, audio, SYNC, key-processing and USB-read measurements. It never records track titles, music paths, serial numbers or network identities. A missing measurement stays unknown.

Each stick holds at most 4 MiB of diary files. Older segments are replaced first, and the previous session's latest segment is kept when a new session starts. Writing pauses during track loads, RAM copies and heavy USB reads. No diary is created on a read-only stick or when less than 64 MiB of free space plus a small write reserve remains. Read-only test sessions save nothing. Normal USB-loader sessions write diary entries when these conditions allow it. Long busy periods and removal can leave gaps.

The diary stays on the sticks. Nothing is sent until you choose to include it in a report.

## Report a problem

When something goes wrong, send a report. It helps fix the problem for everyone.

```nav report-dock-entry Report a problem
```

- **On the player.** Open MODS › **EXTRAS** › **REPORT AN ISSUE**, or push **REPORT THIS** beside an error in the dock. Choose a topic, add words if you like, and send. Offline, the report waits on the stick for your computer. See [Report an issue](extras#report-an-issue).
- **On your computer.** In the XZ Mods app, open **Feedback** at the top right and choose **Report a problem**. Only one box is required, and **My reports** in Feedback shows where your report is afterwards. See [Report a problem or share an idea](desktop-app#report-a-problem-or-share-an-idea).
- **On GitHub.** Open an issue at https://github.com/OpticMystic/XZ-Mods/issues.

Say what you did, what you expected and what happened. The app adds the cleaned-up details itself, and you can see and untick each one. Nothing is sent until you press **Send privately**, and the app posts nothing publicly. From the player, the public GitHub issue is a separate step you submit yourself.
